entries.title: Theme admin list showing commerce.
entries.notes: Capture with only the core Capell stack, Foundation Theme, Layout Builder, and capell-app/theme-commerce installed in the isolated demo harness.
entries.useCase: An administrator confirms the commerce theme is available through the core Themes resource without installing another theme package.

entries.title: Signed admin preview route.
entries.notes: Capture a signed preview URL generated with CreateThemePreviewUrlAction for the seeded commerce theme, site, and page.
entries.useCase: An administrator opens a signed preview URL to inspect a page with the commerce theme applied before publishing the theme choice.

entries.title: Frontend page rendered with commerce theme.
entries.notes: Capture the seeded Stone & Loom page after installing capell-app/theme-commerce and building the Foundation Theme/frontend assets.
entries.useCase: A visitor sees a seeded product page rendered through the commerce navigation, hero, product finder, collections, product grid, catalog, proof, blog teaser, CTA, and footer sections.

entries.title: Commerce homepage.
entries.notes: Capture the retail homepage with merchandising hero, collection tiles, buying-path proof, product rail, and conversion CTA.
entries.useCase: A retailer checks that the theme feels like a buying journey rather than a plain catalogue wrapper.

entries.title: Collection listing.
entries.notes: Capture collection filters, product grid density, merchandising banner, and buyer-intent cards. Requires capell-app/shopify-commerce; show this package note on the captured image.
entries.useCase: A retailer reviews whether shoppers can scan ranges, campaigns, and stock signals quickly.

entries.title: Product detail page.
entries.notes: Capture product detail with gallery, price, variants, stock proof, recommendations, and basket CTA. Requires capell-app/shopify-commerce; show this package note on the captured image.
entries.useCase: A retailer checks that product pages keep purchase intent, proof, and merchandising context together.

entries.title: Lookbook page.
entries.notes: Capture an image-led lookbook with editorial groupings, shoppable cards, and collection pathways. Requires capell-app/media-library; show this package note on the captured image.
entries.useCase: A retailer can sell a range visually without the page becoming Portfolio's work gallery.

entries.title: Buying guide article.
entries.notes: Capture a buying guide article with editorial copy, product recommendations, author details, and collection CTAs. Requires capell-app/blog; show this package note on the captured image.
entries.useCase: A retailer checks that advice content supports purchase decisions instead of becoming a plain blog.

entries.title: Newsletter capture page.
entries.notes: Capture a retail newsletter page with incentive copy, consent messaging, product context, and signup block. Requires capell-app/newsletter; show this package note on the captured image.
entries.useCase: A retailer reviews how the theme converts browsing intent into owned-audience growth.

entries.title: Retail event page.
entries.notes: Capture a retail event page with event details, store location, featured products, and registration CTA. Requires capell-app/events; show this package note on the captured image.
entries.useCase: A retailer can promote launches and in-store events without leaving the merchandising lane.

entries.title: Product search page.
entries.notes: Capture product search with filters, result grid, stock signals, and empty-state recovery. Requires capell-app/search; show this package note on the captured image.
entries.useCase: A shopper can refine buying paths without the page looking like Knowledge search or a standard directory.

entries.title: Promotion campaign page.
entries.notes: Capture a promotion campaign with offer hero, countdown, product groups, and segmented CTAs. Requires capell-app/campaign-studio; show this package note on the captured image.
entries.useCase: A retailer checks that campaigns stay tied to buying paths rather than becoming Agency launch pages.
